title: Enterprise admin access prioritization playbook and triage process
creator: Claire Huang
description:
Purpose: Establish a repeatable intake, scoring, and prioritization process for admin & access requests coming from enterprise prospects and customers (RBAC, SSO/SAML, SCIM, org-wide policies). Goal is to make prioritization transparent to sales/CS, reduce ad-hoc engineering interrupts, and ensure we deliver the minimum secure, auditable implementation needed for deal velocity and compliance.

Scope: Non-bug feature requests relating to organization-level access controls, role model changes, single sign-on onboarding, automated provisioning (SCIM), and org policy enforcement (eg. session length, MFA enforcement, key rotation policies). Excludes ad-hoc support for individual customer SSO configurations and platform incidents.

Proposed intake flow: 1) Sales/CS creates intake using a standardized form (Confluence template + short questionnaire) capturing: customer size, regulated industry, contract stage, must-have vs nice-to-have, estimated seats, required SLA/uptime, data residency constraints, compliance frameworks (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/etc.), and whether the ask impacts audit logs or key management. 2) Triage PM reviews within 3 business days, assigns initial severity and risk score. 3) Triage call with Eng/Trust if score >= threshold. 4) Add to quarterly prioritization board or schedule as fast-follow bugfix depending on scoring.

Scoring rubric (summary): - Compliance sensitivity (0-3): regulated data or legal requirement adds weight. - Deal velocity (0-3): blocks signed contract or PoC. - Customer scale (0-2): number of seats/org size. - Engineering complexity (0-3): estimated effort and cross-team dependencies. - Security exposure (0-3): affects auth, auditability, or secrets. Sum -> Priority band mapping (0-3 low, 4-7 medium, 8-14 high).

Acceptance criteria (minimum for "Done"): - Product: documented role model and UI flows for role creation/assignment; admin console wireframes approved by Design; exported sample SCIM schema. - Security: design review completed and risks logged; audit log entries defined and captured for all admin actions; KMS integration decision recorded if relevant. - Engineering: API contract (OpenAPI snippet) for role/permission endpoints; SSO/SAML metadata flow documented; SCIM provisioning happy path implemented + test harness. - Ops: migration/rollout plan with canary cohort and fallback; per-route telemetry in Console for monitoring.

Rollout recommendation: Canary to 2 paid Dedicated customers and 1 Private deployment (if available) for 2 weeks, measure onboarding success and error rates, then widen to all Dedicated and hosted customers with opt-in for early adopters.

Risk & mitigation: - Complex legacy IAM models from customers -> provide translation mapping service and an initial "custom role" escape hatch. - Security review slippage -> require sign-off gate in PR checklist. - SCIM variance across IdPs -> build robust mapping tests and document common idP quirks.

Next steps: finalize intake form; schedule 1-hour working session with Eng infra, Trust and Design; draft PRD for the highest-scored request queued this cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Design-approved admin console flows for role management
Security review completed with documented mitigations
API contract for RBAC endpoints published
SSO/SAML metadata flow and SCIM happy path implemented and tested
Canary rollout plan and monitoring dashboard configured
